Article Title: Business class passenger wins Rs 1 lakh after Air India gives defective seat on Paris-Delhi flight
Article Text:
AI generated image used for representational purpose

How did the flight turn into a consumer dispute?

Why did the commission rule against Air India?

Suresh Kumar Gupta

Harshali

NEW DELHI: A Delhi district consumer commission, in an order dated July 24, held Air India liable for deficiency in service after a business class passenger was made to travel from Paris to Delhi on a defective seat that would not recline properly.Holding that the airline failed to provide the level of comfort promised to a business class passenger, the commission directed it to pay the passenger Rs 1 lakh as compensation, inclusive of litigation costs.According to the commission's order, complainant Anirudh Wadhwa and his wife were travelling on an Air India business class flight from Paris to New Delhi on October 26, 2015. After boarding the flight, the complainant found that his business class seat was stuck in an uncomfortable position and its controls were not working. Although the cabin crew tried to repair the seat during the flight, they could not fully fix the problem. Since all business class seats were occupied, he had no option but to complete the long journey on the defective seat.The complainants also alleged that the handle of one of their suitcases broke while the baggage was in the airline's custody. They claimed they reported both issues after landing in Delhi, but despite waiting for several weeks and sending a legal notice, the airline did not resolve their complaints.They then approached the consumer commission seeking compensation. Air India denied the allegations, claiming there was no defect in the seat and that the complainants had not produced medical records or sufficient proof of damage to the baggage.The bench comprising presidentand memberfound that the photographs produced by the complainants clearly showed the airline's staff dismantling the business class seat and trying to repair it during the flight. It noted that Air India did not dispute the authenticity of these photographs and also failed to produce any service report or evidence from the cabin crew to show that the seat was functioning properly."The OP cannot deny that complainant no.1's seat did not have some defects which the OP staff were trying to rectify," the commission found.The commission observed that a passenger paying for a business class ticket is entitled to the comfort and facilities promised under that class of travel. It held that forcing the complainant to travel on a defective reclining seat during a long international flight caused mental harassment and inconvenience, for which the airline was liable."The complainant was deprived of a properly functioning reclining seat on a long-haul international flight for which the OP is liable to compensate Complainant No.1," the commission further noted.The commission, however, declined to award compensation for the complainant's alleged health issues, noting that no doctor's certificate or medical records had been produced. It also observed that although the complainants had not produced a bill for the suitcase, the broken handle showed that the baggage had been damaged while in the airline's custody."We allow the complaint and hold the OP guilty of deficiency of service and thus direct the OP to pay a lump sum amount of Rs.1,00,000 to complainant No.1... towards harassment faced by him, inclusive of litigation costs," the bench concluded.
Article Summary: Delhi district consumer commission held Air India liable for deficiency in service. Passenger made to travel from Paris to Delhi on a defective seat that would not recline. Air India denied the allegations, claiming there was no defect in the seat. Commission directed it to pay the passenger Rs 1 lakh as compensation.

Article Title: 'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
Article Text:
Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security

'First selection' after Modi became PM

Shah invokes Lokmanya Tilak's legacy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'Award will inspire those who serve the nation'

Doval accepts award with humility

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security. He said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him.

Article Title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a “strong foundation for progression within the group”. The group has tried to do multiple things — make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay — meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay — while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west — unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers — means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors. The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.“New career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,” said an official.Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.“As AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India. Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,” said teh official.Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as “the primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades. This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.”Following command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. “With 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,” the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.
Article Summary: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%. commanders get the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. First officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express and then move to AI.

Article Title: US judge compares Meta to 'public nuisance,' orders $567m payout over child harm
Article Text:
US judge has ordered Meta to pay $567m in a New Mexico child safety case, ruling that Instagram and Facebook exposed children to harmful content and sexual exploitation

India is facing its own Meta child-safety concerns

Meta has been ordered to pay another $567 million by a US judge over allegations that its social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and failed to adequately protect young users.The ruling by Judge Bryan Biedscheid adds to mounting legal and regulatory pressure on Meta over the way Instagram and Facebook are designed and how they protect children from harmful content, sexual exploitation and potentially addictive use.The judge described Meta as a “public nuisance”, comparing the harm caused to children by its platforms to pollution produced by a factory. The money will be placed in a fund aimed at addressing the damage and preventing further harm.Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, rejected the ruling and said it would appeal.“We disagree with the ruling and will appeal,” a Meta spokesperson said, adding that the company works to keep people safe and remains confident in its record of protecting teenagers online.The latest order follows a $375 million civil penalty previously imposed in the same case, bringing the total financial liability to $942 million.The New Mexico case began with allegations that Meta's platforms exposed young users to sexually explicit material and enabled contact with sexual predators.The court had earlier found that Meta's recommendation systems directed young users towards harmful content and contacts. In the latest phase, the judge ruled that the resulting harms met the legal threshold of a public nuisance.The judge has also ordered a series of measures aimed at limiting risks to children. These include restrictions on interactions between adults and underage users, stronger safeguards against child sexual exploitation, limits on notifications and measures to reduce excessive use of Instagram and Facebook by minors.A significant portion of the $567 million fund — $420 million — will go towards treatment and behavioural-health programmes addressing harms that have already occurred. Other money will support prevention and training for teachers and health professionals.The ruling comes as Meta faces thousands of lawsuits in the US involving alleged harms to children and teenagers. The company has also faced legal challenges over whether the design of its platforms encourages addictive use among young people.The US ruling comes at a particularly relevant moment for Meta in India, where authorities have recently scrutinised the company over child safety on Instagram.In July, India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology ordered Instagram to disable advertisements and content promoting or facilitating access to child sexual abuse material, after reports that such material had appeared in paid advertisements on the platform. The ministry also sought an explanation from Meta.Meta subsequently acknowledged reports about Instagram advertisements in India that violated its policies against child exploitation. The company said its systems had already identified and removed some of the offending advertisements and accounts, while a subsequent investigation led to further removals and blocked URLs. Meta denied that it knowingly targeted such advertisements at users based on inappropriate interests.
Article Summary: US judge has ordered Meta to pay $567m in a New Mexico child safety case. He ruled that Instagram and Facebook exposed children to harmful content and sexual exploitation. The money will be placed in a fund aimed at addressing the damage and preventing further harm.

Article Title: US student visas for Indians drop 62%; CIS report urges scrapping of OPT programme
Article Text:
Indian students dominate OPT programme

What is an OPT programme?

Report urges programme to be scrapped

Chinese student visas also declined

The number of US student visas issued to Indian nationals has fallen by 62% in 2025, according to a new report that also recommends scrapping the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme.The report, authored by George Fishman, Senior Legal Fellow at the Centre for Immigration Studies (CIS), said the US issued 22,149 student visas to Indian nationals in 2025, down sharply from 58,694 issued a year earlier, PTI reported.Despite the decline in new visas, Indian students continued to form the largest group of international students in the US. Data from the Institute of International Education (IIE) showed that 363,019 Indian students were enrolled in US higher education institutions during the 2024-25 academic year, ahead of 265,919 students from China. Together, the two countries accounted for 53% of the 1,177,766 international students studying at the post-secondary levelThe report found that 294,253 international graduates were working in the US under the OPT programme during the 2024-25 academic year. Indian nationals made up the largest share, with 143,740 participants, or 49% of the total. Chinese graduates accounted for 61,981 participants, representing 21%.The Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme is a temporary work authorisation scheme for international students on an F-1 visa in the United States. It allows graduates to work for up to 12 months in a job directly related to their field of study.Students in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) fields can apply for an additional 24-month extension, allowing them to remain and work in the US for a longer period after completing their degree.Fishman argued that the programme should be discontinued, claiming it affects employment opportunities for American workers."I have advocated for the termination of OPT in order to protect the wages and employment opportunities of American students and workers; and end the George W. Bush and Obama administrations' disgraceful use of the OPT program to subvert the will of Congress," he said.He added: "But, short of that, reducing the OPT pipeline of foreign students from India and the PRC, who make up the majority of all OPT participants, will reduce the deleterious effects of OPT on American students and workers."The report noted that student visas issued to Chinese nationals also dropped, falling from 61,075 in 2024 to 40,034 in 2025, a decline of 34%.According to the CIS, the comparison focuses on the May to August period, when most F-1 student visas are issued ahead of the academic year. In 2024, 77% of all F-1 visas granted to Indian students and 76% of those issued to Chinese students were approved during these months.While the report argues that reducing the number of international students entering the OPT pipeline would benefit American workers, any changes to the programme would require action by the US government before taking effect.
Article Summary: US issued 22,149 student visas to Indian nationals in 2025, down sharply from 58,694 issued a year earlier. Indian students continued to form the largest group of international students in the US. Chinese student visas also declined, falling from 61,075 in 2024 to 40,034 in 2025.

Article Title: 'USCIS makes mistakes': Immigration expert breaks down new H-1B, Green Card rule, calls its another step in dismantling legal immigration
Article Text:
Immigration expert says the new USCIS rule will dismantle legal immigration.

What is RFE?

What is NOID?

No scope to correct USCIS' mistake:

AI is not neutral:

Won't make the system quick:

US employers will be impacted:

Fewer fallback options:

Who are not affected?

The USCIS recently announced a major rule change that would affect many categories of visa and Green Card applicants. The agency said that when an applicant submits an application that is not complete, the agency asks for more documents, but now the officers will be empowered to deny the application. The agency said that this will restore integrity to the immigration system and weed out frivolous benefit requests.USCIS has restored officers’ full discretion to deny a benefit request without first issuing an RFE or NOID in various situations. With this updated policy, USCIS can better allocate resources to efficiently make decisions and prevent meritless requests, the agency said. RFE and NOID are two technical terms that offer applicants a small scope to strengthen their case.An RFE (Request for Evidence) is a formal written notice issued by USCIS when an immigration application (such as an H-1B petition, green card, or visa extension) lacks required initial evidence or needs additional documentation before an officer can make a final decision. An RFE is not a denial; it is a temporary pause on the application, giving the applicant or employer a chance to submit missing documents.Notice of Intent to Deny is when the adjudicating officer issues a formal warning that the application has been reviewed, but the officer wants to deny the case unless the applicant comes up with more compelling evidence.The new rule says the adjudicating officer can just reject the application without asking for any additional evidence.Immigration lawyer Jennifer Behm called this another step in dismantling legal immigration and broke down the pitfalls of this new rule in 5 pointsBehm explained that officers can make mistakes; they can overlook evidence, request documents that have already been submitted or misread legal arguments or complex business structures. With zero scope to correct that, there is no chance to rectify the record before a wrongful denial.The attorney said that USCIS already started using AI to go through applications. AI tools flag inconsistencies even before an officer reads the file, and this practice has already led to an overall increase in denial rates."Premium processing is already breaking down. Clients pay a hefty fee for a guaranteed decision window, and cases are routinely blowing past that deadline anyway. USCIS cannot meet the timelines it already charges for. Skipping the RFE step does not fix that. It just means officers will deny faster instead of reviewing faster," Behm said.Those who sponsor H-1B visas or Green Cards will be impacted as they already pay exorbitant filing fees, and now there is a higher chance that the application will be junked, she said.Once denied, the applicants can appeal and wait, and that may take years."The people caught in this are not abstractions. They are employers trying to keep their workforce legal. They are U.S. citizens trying to keep their families together. They deserve a system that gets it right, not one that is simply faster at getting it wrong," Behm explained.The new policy does not apply to overseas visa applicants going through the consular process because those are handled by the US Department of State.The new rule is for applications handled by USCIS, like H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN petitions filed by employers, change or extension of status, Green Card applications, Employment Authorization Documents etc.
Article Summary: USCIS recently announced a major rule change that would affect many categories of visa and Green Card applicants. The agency said that when an applicant submits an application that is not complete, the agency asks for more documents. The new rule says the adjudicating officer can just reject the application without asking for any additional evidence.

Article Title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang to American startups: Working for US government is not a matter of convenience, but basic principle
Article Text:
Meta AI head

Alexandr Wang’s Chinese companies sourcing training data from Silicon Valley firms

AI Czar David Sacks says China's Kimi K3 model is ‘concerning’ for America

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang has called on American startups to treat serving the US government as a fundamental principle rather than a commercial convenience. Reacting to a post shared by Aakash Sabharwal, VP of engineering at Scale AI, Wang said: “Serving the US government should not be a commercial convenience, it must be a bedrock principle for startups. ” Sabharwal, responding to a Forbes report on Chinese companies sourcing training data from Silicon Valley firms, warned that data companies working with the U.S. government should not also serve Chinese AI labs. “American companies should not be selling data to Chinese AI labs. @scale_AI doesn’t do this work, and we have turned down revenue because of it. The companies that do are undermining American AI leadership and risking national security,” he wrote.Alexandr Wang raised concerns after the report by Forbes revealed that Chinese companies are sourcing data from Silicon Valley firms. According to the report, sales teams from Silicon Valley's data-labeling startups encountered eager buyers from China's AI industry at this year's International Conference on Machine Learning in Seoul, with Tencent among the firms circulating detailed requests for training data covering finance, cybersecurity and self-improving AI systems.The investigation found that the same American vendors serving OpenAI, Anthropic, and in some cases the U.S. government, including firms such as Surge AI, Mercor, AfterQuery and Turing, have also supplied Chinese buyers such as Tencent, Ant Group, Alibaba and ByteDance. Citing data-labeling entrepreneurs with visibility into the market, Forbes estimated that the top six Chinese AI labs collectively spend around $500 million a year with American data-labeling companies. The report noted that while the U.S. has restricted China's access to advanced AI chips, it has not placed similar restrictions on the training data and human expertise that shape how AI models learn to perform complex tasks.Meanwhile, in related news, AI Czar David Sacks shared his views on China’s new Kimi K3 artificial intelligence (AI) model, calling its performance “concerning” for American technological dominance. Sacks warned that heavy domestic regulation is crippling US innovation just as overseas rivals catch up, drawing an immediate agreement from billionaire Elon Musk. Sacks comments came soon after Beijing promoted itself as an alternative to American supremacy in AI.“This is concerning. For the first time, a Chinese model Kimi K3 has taken #1 on the Frontend Code Arena and is scoring at or near the frontier on other benchmarks,” Sacks said in a post on X (formerly Twitter). Beijing-backed startup Moonshot AI officially open-sourced a massive 2.8 trillion-parameter system that is actively dethroning top American AI models on global coding benchmarks.“Meanwhile America is tying itself in knots: politicians and bureaucrats are banning new data centers, piling on state regulations, and pushing for new federal agencies to pre-approve frontier models,” Sacks added, purportedly pointing to US government’s decision to restrict Anthropic’s Fable 5 model to non-Americans.“This is how you lose the AI race. The rest of the world won’t play by our rules if we bog ourselves down. Permissionless innovation is how America won the internet and became the technological envy of the world. We can do it again with AI -- while addressing risks in a targeted way -- or we’ll watch our lead evaporate,” he added.
Article Summary: Chinese companies are sourcing training data from Silicon Valley firms, according to a report by Forbes. Meta AI head Alexandr Wang has called on American startups to treat serving the US government as a fundamental principle rather than a commercial convenience. AI Czar David Sacks shared his views on China’s new Kimi K3 artificial intelligence (AI) model, calling its performance ‘concerning’
